owner_posts.post_text:
Self-Esteem and Identity Therapy

Low self-esteem can affect far more than confidence. It can shape your decisions, relationships, ambitions, self-expression, and the way you speak to yourself every day. You may struggle with self-doubt, shame, insecurity, harsh self-criticism, body image concerns, or a deeper confusion about who you are and what you really want. In therapy, I do not offer surface-level confidence advice. I help you understand how these patterns developed, why they keep repeating, and what may be needed for real change. My style is reflective, depth-oriented, and emotionally engaged. Therapy can help you build a more stable sense of self, reduce self-attack, trust your own mind more, make clearer decisions, and begin living with greater confidence, authenticity, and self-respect.

Trauma Therapy

Trauma can continue affecting you long after the painful event is over. It may show up as fear, emotional overwhelm, numbness, mistrust, shame, panic, relationship difficulties, or feeling that the past is still shaping how you respond in the present. Sometimes people do not even think of their experience as trauma, but they know something in them still feels unsettled, guarded, or deeply hurt. In therapy, I work in a paced, respectful, and emotionally containing way. My approach is depth-oriented and sensitive to both emotional safety and the deeper impact of painful experiences. The aim is not to force you to relive what happened, but to help you process it, understand its effects, reduce its hold on your life, and gradually build a stronger sense of safety, stability, and emotional freedom.

Overthinking and OCD Therapy

Overthinking and OCD can leave you feeling trapped inside your own mind. You may keep replaying things, doubting yourself, checking, analysing, seeking reassurance, or struggling with intrusive thoughts that feel upsetting, confusing, or hard to control. These patterns can take away peace of mind, drain energy, and make even simple decisions feel exhausting. In therapy, I work with both the distress you are facing and the deeper emotional patterns that may be keeping these cycles active. My style is careful, non-judgmental, and psychologically in-depth, while still practical enough to help you respond differently in daily life. Therapy can help you reduce the grip of obsessive thinking, feel less controlled by fear and doubt, and regain a greater sense of freedom, clarity, and trust in yourself.

Depression Therapy

Depression is not always obvious from the outside. Sometimes it looks like low mood, tiredness, emptiness, irritability, loss of interest, emotional numbness, crying spells, or simply feeling stuck in survival mode. It can affect motivation, sleep, work, relationships, and your sense of meaning in life. In therapy, I offer a space where your suffering is taken seriously and explored with care. My approach is thoughtful, emotionally attentive, and depth-oriented, with focus on both what is happening now and what may be shaping it underneath. Therapy can help you understand what is weighing you down, reduce self-criticism, reconnect with yourself, and slowly begin to feel more alive, more hopeful, and more able to engage with life again in a meaningful way.

Anxiety Therapy

Anxiety can make daily life feel heavy, tense, and difficult to switch off from. You may find yourself constantly worrying, overthinking, feeling restless, panicky, physically on edge, or expecting something to go wrong even when things seem fine on the surface. Over time, anxiety can affect sleep, work, relationships, confidence, and your ability to feel settled in yourself. In therapy, I help you understand not only the symptoms, but also the emotional patterns and pressures that may be driving them. My style is calm, thoughtful, and depth-oriented, while still practical and grounded. The aim is not just temporary relief, but a deeper sense of steadiness, better emotional regulation, clearer thinking, and the ability to face life with more confidence and less fear.

Anger and Emotional Regulation Therapy

Anger often carries more beneath it than people realise. It may involve frustration, hurt, resentment, helplessness, shame, or feeling repeatedly misunderstood and overwhelmed. When anger shows up as irritability, harsh tone, emotional outbursts, jealousy, impulsive reactions, or difficulty calming down, it can damage relationships, create tension at work or home, and leave you feeling guilty afterward. In therapy, I help you understand not just the anger itself, but what happens inside you before it escalates. My style is direct, thoughtful, and emotionally focused, without being shaming or moralistic. Therapy can help you become less reactive, regulate emotions better, communicate more clearly, and respond with more control, maturity, and steadiness in difficult situations.

A young student I supported during her board exam phase recently wrote to share that she scored 98 and felt that our work together helped her stay calmer, steadier, and able to function well under pressure.

Moments like these are deeply meaningful. Academic performance is never only about intelligence or effort; emotional containment, clarity, and psychological support can make a real difference when it matters most.

Grateful to be trusted in such important phases of people’s lives.

I started therapy with Dr. Tejas Shah during the COVID period in 2020, when I was in a very difficult mental state. Living near Worli sea face, constantly hearing ambulance sirens, reading about COVID, and knowing that older people and those with heart problems were more vulnerable made me extremely anxious. I stopped going out, lost 12 kg, stopped working, and gradually slipped into mild depression. Even basic daily routines became difficult.

Although I was advised to take antidepressants, I was not in favor of psychotropic medication. On the recommendation of my psychologist, I began talk therapy with Dr. Tejas Shah—initially twice a week, and later up to five times a week.

Over time, therapy helped me not only with the fear and distress of that period, but also with long-standing issues of self-doubt, self-criticism, lack of confidence, and feeling “not good enough.” Since 2024, I have gradually reduced therapy to twice a week, which I continue till now (April 2026).

Today, I feel much more relaxed, less self-critical, and more socially at ease. I enjoy conversations, feel more spontaneous, and am much less shy than before. I also see the difference in my professional work. I am calmer with patients, more attentive, and more confident in explaining medical as well as psychological aspects of their condition. I feel I am maturing into a better Psycho-Dermatologist.

At the age of 80, I continue to work, pursue my PhD, journal daily, and stay mentally active. I still have some challenges, such as anxiety before presentations, but I can clearly see how much progress I have made.

I find Dr. Tejas Shah to be a very good analyst—patient, attentive, and a deeply thoughtful listener. His integrative therapy approach has helped bring about meaningful change in my life. I intend to continue therapy with him, now twice a week, for as long as my mind permits.

Square Breathing (Box Breathing): A Simple Technique for Panic Attacks

When anxiety or panic starts to rise, square breathing can help slow your breathing and calm your body’s stress response.

⬜ Step 1: Breathe in through your nose for 4 seconds
⬜ Step 2: Hold your breath for 4 seconds
⬜ Step 3: Breathe out slowly through your mouth for 4 seconds
⬜ Step 4: Hold your breath again for 4 seconds

Repeat this cycle for 1–3 minutes or until you feel calmer.

featured_reviews.name: Seema Krishnadas
featured_reviews.review_text: The ‘ Float to Flight’ session on Autism Spectrum Disorder  was a very insightful and mind opening session. It was the introduction session on Autism, and was presented very well by Mrs. Karthikeyini and Dr. Pawan Mittal. The session covered what exactly is Autism Spectrum Disorder, the early signs & symptoms, causes of Autism, it’s early diagnosis, supportive services like counsellor support to parents of children with ASD, and therapy possibilities in Autism. Both Mrs. karthikeyini and Dr. Mittal have given real life experiences on dealing with children with Autism., who are actually very gifted inspite of their neurodevelopmental disorder. They have shared how important it is for children with Autism to be diagnosed early for better chances of success and how parents of children with Autism should get support and help required and not label their children or allow anyone else to label them either. It is really tough on the parents, yet important to accept it as the new normal. Every child is a blessing!! We should love and nurture them, no matter what. Looking forward to subsequent sessions!!

featured_reviews.name: Urja Jain
featured_reviews.review_text: The session on Autism was not only informative, but worked as an eye opener on the mistakes that we unknowingly make as teachers. Dr. Mittal in this session not only addressed the issues that students with special needs face but also handed out suggestions on how to deal with those in a more inclusive manner, which ensures that while students get the best out of their education and classroom experience they don't feel labelled or alienated. It was something that taught me more about the mindframe of students and parents than my courses on special education.

featured_reviews.name: avanti chandrashekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
We often take kids and their behaviour for granted. Their minute actions and their subtle gestures speak volumes only if we know how to analyse them.
Yesterday was a surefire eye opener to most of us who attended the session " Float to Fly" presented by Mrs. Kartikeyan with invaluable inputs by Dr Pawan Mittal. While being engaging and focussing on the hard hitting realities surrounding special children and conditions such as Autism, the session also cleared a lot of misconceptions about the same.
Without mincing words Dr Mittal put forward the fact that the larger population needs to support and cater to the needs of these gifted children and channelise them in such a way that they get pulled into the main stream with a smooth and effortless transition.
It is imperative for the care givers and family to stand in complete support of these specially gifted kids and raise our voice against any members of the school authority, who give scant regard for the extra care needed to bring them up. After the amazingly wonderful "Float to Fly" session, we are now determined to confront the teachers who label such kids and create a stigma on them.
We are truly grateful to Dr Mittal and Mrs. Karthikeyan for liberally sharing their vast treasure chest of knowledge and bringing a lot of clarity on a complex subject such as Autism. Looking forward to putting this into practice and gaining more insights along our journey.

featured_reviews.name: Poonam Motwani
featured_reviews.review_text: It was a wonderful session. The knowledge shared was very informative. Never had a thought that Autism day can be called as a gifted child day. Practical experiences shared by Dr Mittal helped to understand how to treat and motivate gifted child. Thank you for all the information shared on Autism.

featured_reviews.name: Dhasaradha Senthilnathan
featured_reviews.review_text: NHCA Singapore has been a blessing in my life. Knowledge acquired at the right place from the right person is a wonder. Dr. Pawan Mittal and all the mentors teach the students in the most effective and interesting way. The session on Autism was an eye opening one. Calling the so called special children as GIFTED Children _ the valuable lesson that I learnt yesterday. We must encourage them by saying that you are not special but you are more!!!! A profound lesson for a lifetime. The overall learning about Autism was handled in a very detailed manner. Thank you Dr. Mittal and Mrs.Karthikeyini for the valuable session on Autism. Truly blessed to be a part of NHCA Singapore.

featured_reviews.name: Anjali Saksena
featured_reviews.review_text:
Dr. Pawan Mittal is my Mentor under whose guidance I am doing my Counselling of Child and Adolescent course from NHCA, Singapore.
Dr Mittal's surge of compelling expressions during his ZOOM lecture on 4.4.2022, on his 'Float to Fly' project was an epiphany moment for me.
He has the capability to alchemise his raw, uncoated experiences related to the GIFTED CHILDREN ( children with Autism Spectrum Disorder addressed by him thus) into strong, solid views which have the power to transmute the conservative paradigm of our society  against these ' Gifted Souls' to give birth to a New Normal, if only our hearts and mind were tuned to a receptive frequency towards his viewpoints.
We are thankful to him to come forward and address this profoundly relevant subject which would help all to purge the doubts and negativities, liberate our souls and accept and embrace our ' Gifted Children' lovingly in the mainstream society.
Thank you.
